arxiv-1612-05005.title: A Multilinear Tongue Model Derived from Speech Related MRI Data of the Human Vocal Tract
arxiv-1612-05005.creator: Alexander Hewer, Stefanie Wuhrer, Ingmar Steiner, Korin Richmond
arxiv-1612-05005.description: Abstract We present a multilinear statistical model of the human tongue that captures anatomical and tongue pose related shape variations separately. The model is derived from 3D magnetic resonance imaging data of 11 speakers sustaining speech related vocal tract configurations.

arxiv-2205-07293.title: Searching for cosmic string induced stochastic gravitational wave background with the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array
arxiv-2205-07293.creator: Ligong Bian, Jing Shu, Bo Wang, Qiang Yuan, Junchao Zong
arxiv-2205-07293.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ligong Bian, Jing Shu, Bo Wang, Qiang Yuan, Junchao Zong. We search for stochastic gravitational wave background emitted from cosmic strings using the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array data over 15 years. While we find that the common power-law excess revealed by several pulsar timing array experiments might be accounted for by the gravitational wave background from cosmic strings, the lack of the characteristic Hellings-Downs correlation cannot establish its physical origin yet.

arxiv-2206-00794.title: Sequential Bayesian Neural Subnetwork Ensembles
arxiv-2206-00794.creator: Sanket Jantre, Shrijita Bhattacharya, Nathan M. Urban, Byung-Jun Yoon, Tapabrata Maiti, Prasanna Balaprakash, Sandeep Madireddy
arxiv-2206-00794.description: Abstract Deep ensembles have emerged as a powerful technique for improving predictive performance and enhancing model robustness across various applications by leveraging model diversity. However, traditional deep ensemble methods are often computationally expensive and rely on deterministic models, which may limit their flexibility.

arxiv-2309-01672.title: Perturbative effective field theory expansions for cosmological phase transitions Preprint: NORDITA 2023-037
arxiv-2309-01672.creator: Oliver Gould, and Tuomas V. I. Tenkanen
arxiv-2309-01672.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oliver Gould, and Tuomas V. I. Tenkanen. Guided by previous non-perturbative lattice simulations of a two-step electroweak phase transition, we reformulate the perturbative analysis of equilibrium thermodynamics for generic cosmological phase transitions in terms of effective field theory (EFT) expansions. Based on thermal scale hierarchies, we argue that the scale of many interesting phase transitions is in-between the soft and ultrasoft energy scales, which have been the focus of studies utilising high-temperature dimensional reduction.

arxiv-2402-11004.title: The Evolution of Statistical Induction Heads: In-Context Learning Markov Chains
arxiv-2402-11004.creator: Benjamin L. Edelman 1 , Ezra Edelman 2 , Surbhi Goel 2 , Eran Malach 1 , Nikolaos Tsilivis 3 1 Harvard University, 2 University of Pennsylvania, 3 NYU bedelman@g.harvard.edu, ezrae@cis.upenn.edu surbhig@cis.upenn.edu, emalach@g.harvard.edu, nt2231@nyu.edu
arxiv-2402-11004.description: Abstract Large language models have the ability to generate text that mimics patterns in their inputs. We introduce a simple Markov Chain sequence modeling task in order to study how this in-context learning (ICL) capability emerges. In our setting, each example is sampled from a Markov chain drawn from a prior distribution over Markov chains.

arxiv-2408-02396.title: Unsupervised multi-scale diagnostics
arxiv-2408-02396.creator: Karl Lapo 1 , Sara M. Ichinaga 2 , and J. Nathan Kutz 3
arxiv-2408-02396.description: Abstract The unsupervised and principled diagnosis of multi-scale data is a fundamental obstacle in modern scientific problems from, for instance, weather and climate prediction, neurology, epidemiology, and turbulence. Multi-scale data is characterized by a combination of processes acting along multiple dimensions simultaneously, spatiotemporal scales across orders of magnitude, non-stationarity, and/or invariances such as translation and rotation.

arxiv-2503-11321.title: Leveraging Diffusion Knowledge for Generative Image Compression with Fractal Frequency-Aware Band Learning
arxiv-2503-11321.creator: Lingyu Zhu, Xiangrui Zeng, Bolin Chen, Peilin Chen, Yung-Hui Li, Shiqi Wang
arxiv-2503-11321.description: Abstract By optimizing the rate-distortion-realism trade-off, generative image compression approaches produce detailed, realistic images instead of the only “sharp-looking” reconstructions produced by rate-distortion optimized models. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based generative image compression method injected with diffusion knowledge, obtaining the capacity to recover more realistic textures in practical scenarios.

arxiv-2509-12704.title: NORA: A Nephrology-Oriented Representation Learning Approach Towards Chronic Kidney Disease Classification
arxiv-2509-12704.creator: Mohammad Abdul Hafeez Khan, Twisha Bhattacharyya, Omar Khan, Noorah Khan[0.1cm], Alina Aziz Fatima Khan, Mohammed Qutub Khan, Sujoy Ghosh Hajra, [0.2cm] Florida Institute of Technology, USA, [0.1cm] Edgewood Jr./Sr. High School, USA Shadan Institute of Medicine Sciences, India, [0.1cm] Riverside Nep
arxiv-2509-12704.description: Abstract Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) affects millions of people worldwide, yet its early detection remains challenging, especially in outpatient settings where laboratory-based renal biomarkers are often unavailable. In this work, we investigate the predictive potential of routinely collected non-renal clinical variables for CKD classification, including sociodemographic factors, comorbid conditions, and urinalysis findings.

pmc-10582056.title: Identification of key biomarkers and associated pathways of pancreatic cancer using integrated transcriptomic and gene network analysis
pmc-10582056.creator: Majji Rambabu, Nagaraj Konageni, Karthick Vasudevan, K R Dasegowda, Anand Gokul, Sivaraman Jayanthi, Karunakaran Rohini
pmc-10582056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Pancreatic cancer shows malignancy around the world standing in 4th position for causing death globally. This cancer is majorly divided into exocrine and neuroendocrine where exocrine pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is observed to be nearly 85% of cases. The lack of diagnosis of pancreatic cancer is considered to be one of the major drawbacks to the prognosis and treatment of pancreatic cancer patients.

pmc-10615039.creator: Candice Oster, Sonia Hines, Chris Rissel, Dennis Asante, Jyoti Khadka, Katrin M Seeher, Jotheeswaran Amuthavalli Thiyagarajan, Christopher Mikton, Theresa Diaz, Vivian Isaac

pmc-10719483.title: AZD9567 versus prednisolone in patients with active rheumatoid arthritis: A phase IIa, randomized, double‐blind, efficacy, and safety study
pmc-10719483.creator: Jacob M. van Laar, Alejhandra Lei, Mary Safy‐Khan, Joachim Almquist, Graham Belfield, Karl Edman, Lisa Öberg, Bastian R. Angermann, Inken Dillmann, Pia Berntsson, Damla Etal, Ian Dainty, Carol Astbury, Maria G. Belvisi, Szilárd Nemes, Adam Platt, Susanne Prothon, Sara Samuelsson, Petter Svanberg, Ch
pmc-10719483.description: Oral corticosteroid use is limited by side effects, some caused by off‐target actions on the mineralocorticoid receptor that disrupt electrolyte balance. AZD9567 is a selective, nonsteroidal glucocorticoid receptor modulator. The efficacy, safety, and tolerability of AZD9567 and prednisolone were assessed in a phase IIa study. Anti‐inflammatory mechanism of action was also evaluated in vitro in monocytes from healthy donors.

pmc-11350795.title: Enhancing the Viability of a Small Giant Panda Population Through Individual Introduction From a Larger Conspecific Group: A Scientific Simulation Study
pmc-11350795.creator: Yuzhen Zhang, Jiabin Liu, Jiaojiao Yu, Cheng Li, Xing Zhao, Li Mo, Wei Wu, Yulin Gai, Qiang Xu, Jiubin Ni, Limin Shen, Haijun Gu, Jindong Zhang, Dunwu Qi, Xiaodong Gu, Miho Inoue-Murayama
pmc-11350795.description: Simple SummaryIndividual quantity is the guarantee of the long-term survival of a population. Currently, approximately 70% of the 33 local populations of wild giant pandas (Aliuropoda melanoleuca) face the risk of extinction. We studied four typical populations, from Tangjiahe, Wanglang, Liziping, and Daxiangling, and attempted to translocate individuals from large populations to enhance the viability of small populations.

pmc-11504226.title: Somatostatin Receptor Type 2 as a Potential Marker of Local Myocardial Inflammation in Myocardial Infarction: Morphologic Data on Distribution in Infarcted and Normal Human Myocardium
pmc-11504226.creator: Vyacheslav V. Ryabov, Andrey A. Trusov, Maria A. Kercheva, Aleksandra E. Gombozhapova, Julia N. Ilyushenkova, Ivan V. Stepanov, Mikhail V. Fadeev, Anna G. Syrkina, Svetlana I. Sazonova
pmc-11504226.description: Nuclear imaging modalities can detect somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) in vivo as a potential marker of local post-MI inflammation. SSTR2+ macrophages are thought to be the main substrate for SSTR-targeted radioimaging. However, the distribution of SSTR2+ cells in the MI patients’ myocardium is unknown.

pmc-13111936.title: Risk Factors for Adverse Circulatory and Respiratory Events in Patients Undergoing Esophageal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection Under Dexmedetomidine-Based Sedation
pmc-13111936.creator: Kenshi Matsuno, Hideaki Miyamoto, Sayoko Tayama, Kotaro Waki, Akira Yamasaki, Yoki Furuta, Ryosuke Gushima, Hideaki Naoe, Yasuhito Tanaka
pmc-13111936.description: Background/AimsSufficient sedation is important when performing an endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for an esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and dexmedetomidine (DEX) is being increasingly used. ESD is often performed in elderly patients and those with comorbidities. Therefore, adverse events (AEs) in the circulatory and respiratory systems remain a clinical concern.

pmc-13402427.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps and acute kidney injury: a narrative review
pmc-13402427.creator: Shuyuan Zhou, Jiawei Lu, Jie Zheng, Yunqiang Liao, Si Chen, Haizhen Wu, Jiahui Xiong, Xiaosheng Li, Yang Tang
pmc-13402427.description: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are complex, network-like structures comprising chromatin filaments bound to various antimicrobial proteins. While they play a role in host defence under physiological conditions, there is evidence to suggest that excessive production or impaired clearance of NETs may contribute to the pathological progression of acute kidney injury (AKI).
